<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The script `arculator.sh` is a simple launcher script that ensures user-specific data is set up and then executes the main application. It first defines system and user data directories, then checks if the user directory contains the application data. If not, it copies the system-wide data from `/usr/share/arculator` to the user's local directory. This is a common pattern for applications that need per-user writable data while being installed system-wide.

The script uses safe practices: it sets `set -e` to exit on errors, properly quotes all variable expansions to prevent word splitting, and only copies from a system-protected location (`/usr/share`) to a user-controlled one. The execution of `./arculator` occurs within the user's data directory, but this is the same binary name installed in the shared directory, and no network operations, dynamic downloads, or unsafe evaluations (like `eval` or `curl|sh`) are performed. There is no obfuscation, unexpected file manipulation, or privilege escalation.

This script behaves consistently with standard application launcher patterns in Linux desktop environments and does not exhibit any characteristics of a supply-chain attack.
</details>
